types.title: Wrong number or arithmetic
types.definition: A number, sum, date, count or price that is wrong and can be proven wrong from the material itself or from a listed source.
types.example: A caption adds 14.80 + 3.50 + 2.00 and states the total as 21.30 instead of 20.30.

types.title: Claim contradicted by the material or a source
types.definition: A statement of fact that the material elsewhere, or a listed source, shows to be false.
types.example: A post says the service works in Estonia while the offer page and the site say Finland only.

types.title: Two places in the work contradict each other
types.definition: Two parts of the work say incompatible things about the same subject; at least one of them must be wrong.
types.example: The strategy section promises 38 short videos while the plan table lists 18.

types.title: Language error
types.definition: A grammar, spelling or diacritics error, a word in the wrong script, or a calque that a native speaker of the text's language (for example Russian, Spanish or English) will notice.
types.example: Spanish 'la problema' instead of the correct 'el problema'.

types.title: Broken step on the path to the goal
types.definition: The reader cannot complete the intended action: a call-to-action word that the system will not recognise, a wrong link target, a reference to a form or button that does not exist.
types.example: The reader is asked to send the code word in Cyrillic letters while the reply bot only reacts to the Latin word.

types.title: Violates an explicit line of the owner's task
types.definition: The work does something the owner's task explicitly forbids, or does it differently from an explicit instruction in the task.
types.example: The task says every post must lead to the request form; one post sends readers to a third-party listing site.

types.title: Contradicts a stated rule, policy, platform rule or law
types.definition: The work contradicts a rule written in the material, the site's own policy, a platform's rules or the law.
types.example: A post promises a guarantee although the material's own rules forbid promising a guarantee.

types.title: Required element removed
types.definition: A deliverable, a call to action or one item of a required series is missing although the task or the material requires it.
types.example: One post of a series that must all end with a call to action has its closing call to action removed.

types.title: Required caveat, disclaimer or attribution removed
types.definition: A caveat, disclaimer or source attribution that the claim next to it needs has been removed.
types.example: A price comparison loses its sentence saying that prices are examples from a given date.

types.title: Rendered visual defect
types.definition: A defect that is visible only in the rendered output: a missing logo, overlapping text, unreadable contrast. Needs a rebuild of the rendered files and is used only when visual canaries are allowed for the run.
types.example: The footer logo is missing from one slide of a series where every other slide has it.
